paragraphs: The Government wants hospitals to charge less for parking. It wants a limit of €10 a day.
Health Minister Jennifer Carroll MacNeill wrote a letter to a group of TDs in the Dáil. She said the HSE will look at parking prices in every hospital.
Some hospitals charge more than €10 now. St Vincent's Hospital in Dublin charges €17 a day. That is the highest price.
Hospitals made €17.8 million from parking last year. Since 2020, they made more than €73.5 million.
The idea of a €10 limit is not new. A report asked for it in 2018. The HSE says parking money pays for repairs and security. The review will end in early 2027.

The Government has asked the Health Service Executive (HSE) to limit hospital parking charges to €10 a day. The plan would help patients and visitors who often pay high prices when they go to hospital.

Health Minister Jennifer Carroll MacNeill explained the plan in a letter to the Dáil's Public Accounts Committee. She said the HSE will carry out a national review of parking charges. It should be finished in the first three months of 2027.
At the moment, four hospitals charge more than €10 a day. The committee's chairman, Sinn Féin TD John Brady, said St Vincent's Hospital in Dublin has the highest charge, at €17 a day.

Parking is a big source of money for hospitals. Fees brought in €17.8 million last year, and more than €73.5 million since 2020. Cork University Hospital collected the most, almost €12 million, followed by St James's, Beaumont and University Hospital Limerick.

The €10 limit is not a new idea. A review in 2018 recommended it, together with cheaper passes for people who visit often. However, these ideas were never fully put in place. Now the top official at the Department of Health has written to the head of the HSE, Anne O'Connor, to ask for action.

The HSE says the parking money is important. It pays for repairs, loans for new car parks, security and sometimes other hospital costs. The minister said the review will look at the cost of any changes and at how to keep funding steady.
The Government wants the Health Service Executive (HSE) to cap hospital parking fees at €10 a day, in a move aimed at easing the financial pressure on patients and their families.

In a letter to the Dáil Public Accounts Committee, Health Minister Jennifer Carroll MacNeill said the HSE would conduct a national review of car parking charges, which is due to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.

Four hospitals currently charge patients and visitors more than €10 a day. According to the committee's chairman, Sinn Féin TD John Brady, St Vincent's Hospital in Dublin has the highest rate, at €17 per day.

Parking fees generated €17.8 million last year, and figures released in response to parliamentary questions show that hospitals have earned more than €73.5 million from their car parks since 2020. Cork University Hospital topped the list with almost €12 million, ahead of St James's, Beaumont and University Hospital Limerick.

The proposed limit dates back to a review carried out in 2018, which also called for flexible passes and discounts for frequent visitors. Those recommendations were never fully implemented. The secretary general of the Department of Health, Derek Tierney, has now written to HSE chief executive Anne O'Connor asking for them to be put into effect.

The HSE argues that car park income covers maintenance, loan repayments on upgrades and site security. The minister said the review would weigh affordability against the financial implications and the need for sustainable funding.
The Government is pressing the Health Service Executive (HSE) to impose a €10 daily ceiling on hospital parking charges, a long-standing grievance among patients and the relatives who visit them.

Health Minister Jennifer Carroll MacNeill set out the position in correspondence with the Dáil Public Accounts Committee, confirming that the HSE will undertake a nationwide review of car parking fees, with findings expected in the first quarter of 2027.
At present, four hospitals exceed the proposed threshold. The committee's chairman, Sinn Féin TD John Brady, has singled out St Vincent's Hospital in Dublin, where motorists pay as much as €17 a day.

The sums involved are far from trivial. Parking yielded €17.8 million last year, and replies to parliamentary questions reveal that more than €73.5 million has flowed into hospital coffers from car parks since 2020. Cork University Hospital accounted for the lion's share, at close to €12 million, followed by St James's, Beaumont and University Hospital Limerick.

Strikingly, the €10 cap is hardly a fresh proposal: it was first recommended in a 2018 review, alongside flexible and concessionary passes for frequent visitors, yet those measures have languished ever since. Derek Tierney, secretary general of the Department of Health, has now urged HSE chief executive Anne O'Connor to implement the outstanding recommendations.

The HSE, for its part, maintains that parking revenue underpins maintenance, loan repayments on upgraded facilities and site security. The minister acknowledged that the review must strike a balance between affordability, the financial consequences of lower charges and the search for a sustainable funding model.
